::: {.why}
This is the one measurement in the phase that cannot be repeated, so everything about the strategy has to be frozen before you start it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Freeze every parameter and run the strategy once on the held-out period.
- Report the result whatever it is, alongside what the in-sample period predicted.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Freeze the configuration in a file so it is auditable: universe, formation window, selection rule, threshold derivation, hedge ratio method, cost assumption. Commit it. Then run the strategy once on the held-out period and record the result.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Run the same frozen configuration on 500 synthetic universes from qlib.simulate that contain no true cointegration, and report the distribution of Sharpe ratios it produces. Your out-of-sample number belongs somewhere in that distribution, and where it falls is the actual result of milestone 3.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The pairs strategy is frozen in a committed configuration file and run once out of sample, with its result placed against the distribution the same procedure produces on synthetic data containing no relationships at all.
:::

## Resources

- [Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu (2017) — The Probability of Backtest Overfitting](https://escholarship.org/content/qt4w1110bb/qt4w1110bb.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}
- [Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (1999) — Pairs Trading (NBER w7032)](https://www.nber.org/papers/w7032) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
The frozen configuration file, the single out-of-sample result, and the null distribution from 500 synthetic universes.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your out-of-sample Sharpe is 0.4 and the synthetic null distribution has a 95th percentile of 0.6. What have you learned?
:::
